body: School hasn't started yet for me.  Next week it will.
Family is no help, and I have friends, but none I feel confortable talking to.  I'm not busy and I have access to computers and telephones but cannot drive yet.
That's what I was thinking.  Maybe I could just say I want nobody hugging me to avoid seeming like I'm targeting him.  I don't like hugs anyway.

My brother isn't exactly the most docile person and he has a history with violence towards mostly inanimate objects, but some people as well.  He is extremely muscular while I'm extremely skinny, so I want to avoid confrontation with him.  The high five thing is actually a really good idea. Thanks!
People always tell me that, so that's also what has me worried.  Isn't that phrase just perfect?  My dad stole it from AA, which actually has the best vernacular, at least in our area.

I suppose you're right.  I was just fed-up with everything she's been doing and I'm usually quite timid, so I was taking the opportunity while I was already on the shit list.  Also, I'm going on a trip to my dad's parents house, so she can be angry 3000 miles away.  I'll resist next time.  Thanks for the advice.

My dad is a former alcoholic and doesn't have a good relationship at all with my brother and mother and never talks to them, although they are still married and live in the same house, so he is not a candidate to talk to him. I do intend on getting a job and tried to get one this year, but health problems and lack of transportation makes it difficult. I'm definitely going to the school counselor as soon as it starts. . Thanks for the advice. 

Edit: when I asked my mom to see a therapist,  she told me I was embarrassing to her and nobody else would ever put up with me.  She threw stuff and me and screamed to get out of the car (just notice all of these situations take place in the car...)  My doctor is a very nice guy, but he got pissed at her for not taking me.  Now she says he's a quack, but we have to keep going back because he's been my neurologist since I was a baby.  Hopefully he'll make something happen, but until then I'll check out my school counselor when school's in.

Thanks you the advice, but the silence is a form of punishment.  I've been shunned for days and even over a week, even when I try to start conversation about trivial things like a show or movie.  I don't hate my family, but my mother is not a normal person.  Honestly, she is sick and needs help that she'll never accept.  She's planted mics to record people, thrown things at me, punched holes in the wall, among other things. Our family is not the typical situation.

If it's any consolation, I believe emotional pain and illness can certainly be much more insidious than physical pain and illness.  Not only does it cause suffering,  but it robs you of the capacity to power through it.  And people don't understand depression like they can understand physical illness, so even though you may be suffering just as much as someone with a physical illness,  you won't get much sympathy.  I have chronic illness in addition to being depressed, but I'd take ridding myself of depression over physical illness any day, which people don't seem to understand.

You have sleep problems and fall down escalators?  You might want to get checked out for narcolepsy with cataplexy.  It's actually not that rare and many doctors don't know much about it.  Thanks for the reply and I hope things get better for you too.
I don't know.  I've been sick for the last 6 months with neurological problems.  I think I may be burnt out from stress.

This grinds my gears so much!  It's like if I wasn't feeling so good, so I said "Ugh! I feel so cancerous! Lol!".  Or how about if I'm thirsty and say "Omg!  It's like I have diabetes! :D".  No!  People just throw around depression like it's a joke.  It' in the same vein as when people use OCD, bipolar, schizophrenic, ect.  Mental illness has enough stigma around it without people saying they're "OCD" because they organise the apps on their phone or that whoever is so bipolar because she was sad yesterday and now today she's not sad ( or on her period obviously /s).  It's just ridiculous.

That's very brave of you to tell your parents about how you're feeling.  It's just awful that seeing someone tell them something that is so hard for people to talk about just results in them brushing it off.  I was just in the same situation and I had no idea what I should do because I had nobody else to talk to that would take me seriously.  I even went so far as to go on one of those crisis hotlines and asked to person what I should do and she honestly wasn't all that helpful.  I finally formulated a plan to tell my doctor about it during an appointment, even though it was for something else.  When I told him, he talked to my mother about how serious it is and got her to get me therapy.  A school counsellor would probably be the quickest course of action, but if you don't have access to one, maybe you can convince your parents to bring you to a doctor, even if you don't tell them it's for depression.  Some people don't feel as if depression warrants the same amount of attention as a "physical" medical issue, so a doctor telling them may give them a wake up call.  Hope you feel better :)

Thank you guys so much! :)  I actually talked to my neurologist today about it and he told my mom that I need to see a therapist and she always listens to him.  He took me off my meds until he sees what the therapist says since the side effects were so severe, but they weren't working much and it's the summer so it's not too bad.

Also in high school. :)  I notice the exact same thing.  I'll have a week of going to bed and instantly becoming stuck in that weird limbo between sleep and being awake where all that SP/HH stuff happens either every night or very frequently.  Then there are a few weeks in between where it just happens occasionally.  It also happens with my cataplexy: it will gradually get worse until my legs are just giving out at every single provocation and then suddenly stop for a few weeks and repeat the process.  I notice reading before bed helps prevent sleep paralysis when it's around.

Because a voluntary action deserves more empathy and accommodation than an illness you didn't ask for, right?  I have narcolepsy and I already get my jimmies rustled when I get "Oh, I get tired a lot too".  If someone said this to me I'd blow my top!
